# intrastate

> A Go CLI that makes workflow state transitions explicit, reviewable,
> and deterministic. A flow is authored once as a transition model — a
> TOML document of tags, rules, guards, and writes — and callers
> navigate it by asking the CLI rather than reimplementing the flow in
> a skill, script, or agent. Given the same model, state, tags, and
> recognized outcome, the answer is the same every time: one legal
> plan, or one typed refusal.

The binary is authoritative and self-describing. Prefer asking it over
reading any file here — a file is a snapshot, the binary is the build
you actually have:

```sh
intrastate --help-all      # every command's full reference
intrastate <cmd> --help-all
intrastate <cmd> --as=json # one terminal JSON envelope per run
```

## Commands

- `intrastate flow`: Drive a transition model from a skill
- `intrastate flow init-state`: Seed owned state from the model's [initial] root
- `intrastate flow next`: Report the candidate rules the supplied state can take
- `intrastate flow read-state`: Report what the declared read accessors see
- `intrastate flow resolve`: Map one recognized outcome to exactly one plan
- `intrastate flow set-state`: Apply planned owned-tag writes, verified by read-back
- `intrastate graph`: Export a model's normalized graph as a document
- `intrastate lint`: Check a transition model against the graph invariants
- `intrastate version`: Print build version, commit, and date

## Docs

- [CLI reference](docs/cli-reference.md): every command, flag, and
  extended body — generated from the command tree.
- [Model authoring](docs/model-authoring.md): how to author a
  transition model in TOML — the model class, a decision table's
  cells, and the escape row. Not derivable from the CLI surface.
- [Output contract](docs/cli-output-contract.md): worked JSON
  payloads and the rationale behind the envelope shape.
- [README](README.md): what it is, install, and a first invocation.

## Optional

- [Decision records](docs/rdr/): the locked design decisions behind
  the contracts above. History and rationale; the code is the source
  of truth.
- [CONTRIBUTING](CONTRIBUTING.md): layout, the contract every verb
  follows, and the build targets.
